title: Ship the quest-board mod in the opum-quest plugin (OPAG-1074)
description: Operator instruction, 2026-10-02 (relayed by opum-doc as ODOC-OP-2026-10-02-10; tracked in opum-agent as OPAG-1074): build the Quest board mod and ship it in the opum-quest plugin. Design brief: opum-doc docs/reference/quest-board-mod-design-brief.md, merged by opum-ai/opum-doc#619 and read at opum-doc dev 4fbc7578. Prototype: opum-docs session-local dev-mods folder, copied in here as the starting point. The mod is a hooks module plus its contract and tests, shipped inside the opum-quest plugin cut from this repository, with the marketplace pin moving to the release that carries it. Two questions stay with the operator and are not decided here: edits from a fleet view, and the actor identity for pane edits. This task covers the build and its landing only; the release is its own task.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The opum-quest plugin ships the quest-board hooks module: hooks/hooks.json names one module, and .claude-plugin/plugin.json declares the modules state contract and the pane actor option.

claude plugin validate on the repository root reports the plugin valid on the builds pinned Claude Code version, and the module typechecks against the engine declaration with no errors; both exact commands and their results are recorded on the task.
The mod test suite passes under claude plugin test across the terminal and desktop surfaces, and a repo gate runs it so a failing mod test fails the gate rather than passing unrun.
The fleet view reads a discovered repository set rather than a hardcoded list, configurable through the plugins userConfig, with the sessions own repository always included.

The board offers the repository-true read (quest task list --across-refs) as a toggle, marks a task whose states disagree across refs, and shows an incomplete coverage read as incomplete rather than as an empty result.

A pane write happens only in the sessions own repository, through Quest lifecycle commands, with an explicit actor on every write and --if-revision on field edits; a test asserts the argv of each write.
The repositorys own checks exit 0 with the mod files present, and the repo test suite neither collects nor breaks on the mod test files.
The repositorys lore docs describe the mod and record its design decisions, and lore check exits 0.
The change lands on dev by a squash-merged pull request that cites the run validating its deliverable, and this task is closed in that PR.

plan: Branch feat/QCLI-431-quest-board-mod off origin/dev, carrying this task record on the first commit (orchestrator, 2026-10-02).

Copy the opum-doc prototype into the plugin root: hooks/hooks.json, hooks/register.tsx, types/index.d.ts, mod tests; rename the state namespace and mount name to the plugin opum-quest; merge userConfig and the types contract into .claude-plugin/plugin.json.

Apply the brief recommendations: repository-true reads via quest task list --across-refs as a toggle with cross-ref state merge and coverage surfaced; repository discovery through userConfig with the sessions own repo always included; keep the write boundary, the Quest lifecycle commands and the mobile line.

Add scripts/mod-test.mjs: stage the plugins shipped files into a temp dir and run claude plugin validate, claude plugin test and tsc against the engine types there; wire it into bun run check and into prepublish source gates, installing the pinned CLI in the CI job.
Keep the repos own suite off the mod tests (bun --path-ignore-patterns) and gitignore the engine-written .claude-plugin/types.

Write the lore Reference doc for the mod, recording the execution choices and the alternatives rejected (layout with the staged-files runner over a git-subdir move; the refs toggle default; discovery) and the deferred keyboard card movement. No ADR: component design records are the operators, and the orchestrator ruled on 2026-10-02 that these are execution choices recorded here and on this task. lore check exits 0.
Record validate/test/tsc/check evidence on this task, open the PR into dev, and close this task in it.
implementationNotes: SCOPE AND RECORDING SHAPE, settled 2026-10-02 with the orchestrator before building. (1) Keyboard card movement on the kanban (brief recommendation 5) is DEFERRED, and that is the orchestrators scope call: the list tab already carries every edit, and card movement is new behaviour and new test surface the operator did not ask for; opum-doc is being told so the operator can bring it back. (2) The fleet-edit question from the brief is NOT REACHED: v1 keeps the fleet view read-only, so there is nothing to decide; recorded as deliberately out of scope rather than unfinished. (3) The actor identity for pane edits is the operators and is still open; it goes to the orchestrator as an A/B when the manifests default is final. (4) No ADR for the layout or the test-runner choice: under the operating models design authority every ADR is the operators, including one about a single component, so these are recorded as execution choices in the repos own Reference doc and here, with the alternatives that were rejected and why.
